## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy**, held by the VIX level and nothing else, for a third consecutive read. **VIX 16.80 is inside the 15–22 band and FELL 2.33% on the morning of the decision; VXN 22.26 is also inside.** **No Stage-4 threshold has fired: VIX needs +19.05% to reach 20, VXN needs +12.31% to reach 25, NDX needs −1.86%, HY OAS needs +54bp.** **The "breadth deteriorating" half of the Stage-4 definition remains satisfied — roughly 33.5% of S&P 500 members are above their 50-day average as of 2026-09-15** ([thetrading.tools](https://www.thetrading.tools/market-breadth)) **— but the VIX condition is explicit and it is not met.** **Scoring conservatively, between Stage 3 and Stage 4 I take the one the stated thresholds support: Stage 3.** **Third read running where one number, and only one number, separates the two — and that number is now moving away from Stage 4 rather than toward it.**
- **Stage Anchor:** **2026-08-28 — Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote**, which moved implied September hike odds from roughly 30% to a majority ([CNBC 2026-08-28](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)). **The anchor resolves today at 14:00 ET, at 92–93% implied.** The **US–Iran conflict** (from 2026-02-28) amplifies through the oil-and-yields channel.
- **Position:** **Week 3 of the rate-repricing leg — decision day.** Stage-3 range confirmed across fifteen consecutive reads (08-28 through 09-16). **Whatever this leg becomes, it stops being a "waiting" regime this afternoon.**
- **Confidence:** **High.** Five lenses bearish (Macro −2, Breadth −2, Cross-asset −2, Geopolitical −2, Dealer flow −1), none bullish, two neutral. **No degradation cap: WebSearch was available, the option chain fetched, and macro, breadth, sentiment, energy and geopolitical inputs were all verified today.**
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ **30,000** (+3.67%) **with** VXN below **19** (−14.65%); **or** a dovish FOMC surprise today — no hike against 92–93% odds, or a hike with 2027 dots showing no further moves; **or** Brent sustainably below **$92** (−14.18%); **or** a concluded US–China tariff-reduction announcement.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above **20** (+19.05% — **still the sole hinge of the stage classification**); **or** **VXN > 25** (+12.31%); **or** NDX < **28,400** (−1.86%); **or** **HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%** (from 2.71% / 0.80%, both 09-14).

## Regime Verdict
A Stage-3 range held together by a VIX that is *falling* into the first Fed rate increase since July 2023 — with the 10-year at 5.00% and its highest since 2007, an oil trigger now confirmed fired, breadth at roughly a third of the index above its 50-day, TQQQ sitting 0.83% above the bottom of its own four-week range, and no lens in this report positive — at **High** confidence.

**Data note.** WebSearch was available and the option chain fetched successfully, so this is a full read with no degradation cap. **Resolved since last read: the Brent row (Finding 9) — the engine's 09-15 print of $101.15 was wrong and has silently corrected.** **New and unresolved: the Saudi East-West pipeline. CNBC reported on 09-15 that it was pumping again at full 7 mb/d capacity; today's reporting says there is "still no clear timeline" for resumption and that Saudi Arabia has cancelled several September deliveries to European customers** ([TradingEconomics/Brent, Sep 16](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil)). **Those cannot both be current. I have not resolved it and have not let either version move a score.** **Still stale:** HY OAS 2.71% and IG OAS 0.80% carry 2026-09-14 stamps (better than last read's 09-11, and they now cover the AI selloff session). **Never retrieved in any read:** AAII, CFTC COT, margin debt, ETF flows, Citi Economic Surprise, insider/buyback activity, Copper/Gold, transports. **NAAIM remains paywalled since 2026-08-01.**

## Diverging Signals

**First, and it reframes today's main event: the market is already priced ABOVE the Fed's own published path, so the dot plot can surprise in either direction.** **June's dots implied a 3.8% funds rate by end-2026 — one quarter-point hike, which is what is expected today. But futures now price roughly 4.2% by December 2026 and about 4.6% by September 2027** ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/fed/fed-rate-hike-warsh-dot-plot-inflation)). **Yesterday I framed the risk as one-sided: "the repricing risk is entirely in whether the new dots show MORE." That framing was incomplete, and this number corrects it.** **The market has already moved past the June dots. If the September dots come in at or near where the market is, that is confirmation. If they come in BELOW — showing this as a one-off adjustment rather than a path — the market has to unwind roughly 40bp of 2026 pricing, which would be a dovish surprise from a hawkish action. Both tails are live, and that is a different risk shape from a purely hawkish one.**

**Second: the AI story and the rates story have merged, and that matters specifically for a leveraged Nasdaq instrument.** **Bloomberg names heavy corporate debt issuance by AI companies as one reason long-term yields are rising — the issuance is crowding out primary dealer capital allocation** ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/us-10-year-treasury-yields-rise-to-highest-since-2007)). **At the same time, the AI-slowdown agreement that took the chip index down 5.9% on Monday is a challenge to the earnings those investments are meant to produce** ([Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/09/15/ai-development-slowdown-what-it-means-for-nvidia-micron-and-other-chip-stocks/), [SBS](https://news.sbs.co.kr/english/article.do?news_id=N1008753141)). **In plain terms: the same capital-expenditure boom is simultaneously pushing up the discount rate applied to the NDX and having its payoff questioned by the people running it. Those are not two risks that might both happen. They are one mechanism working from both ends, and it lands hardest on the index this instrument tracks 3×.** **Jensen Huang pushed back this morning — "don't need AI regulation, leave safety to us"** ([Yahoo live](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-september-16-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-080356525.html)) — **which is a data point that the argument is contested, not that it is over.**

**Third: the volatility market and the gold market disagree about today.** **VIX fell 2.33% to 16.80 into a first hike since July 2023, and SKEW fell 3.60% to 146.61 — both say "this is handled".** **Gold rose 1.27% to $4,387.80, its first real bid in four reads — that says someone wants protection they have not wanted all week.** **Either the equity-vol market is right that the decision is fully discounted, or the metal is right that the projections are not. I cannot tell you which, and the honest observation is that these two markets have been in agreement for the last several reads and are not today.**

**Fourth: credit remains the calmest thing in this report, and it is now less stale than it was.** **HY OAS 2.71% and IG OAS 0.80%, stamped 2026-09-14 — so they DO now cover Monday's semiconductor selloff and the first break above 5% on the 10-year.** **HY widened 6bp over that period. Six basis points is essentially nothing. A credit market that absorbs a 5.9% drop in the leadership sector and a 2007-high long bond by widening 6bp is telling you the stress has not reached the funding channel.** **That is the single strongest argument this report has against its own conclusion, and it deserves to be stated as clearly as the bearish evidence.**

**Fifth: the news daemon mis-signed a story again, in exactly the way it did on 09-11.** **It reads SHOCK / 42.0. Its top signal, at impact 10.0, is "U.S. and China soften trade war as Trump and Xi discuss tariff cuts" — which is a DE-ESCALATION.** **The second and third signals are US–Canada trade-war cost stories at impact 7.5.** **A magnitude-only model cannot tell the difference between a trade war starting and a trade war ending, and it scored the most bullish headline of the week as the largest shock in the set.** **This is the same failure mode as 09-11 (SHOCK on a de-escalation), and it is the fourth consecutive read with a daemon defect.** **I have set `news_shock_score: 4` against the daemon's 42.0, calibrated on the realized move: NQ futures are UP 0.56% this morning with the tariff story in the tape. Between 4 and 5 I take the lower.**
